code.originalText: Two-week review, five days after the sick visit: kidney function and potassium, medicine doses, lipids, and cardiac rehabilitation adapted to the ocean

text.paragraph: Two-week review, five days after the sick visit. [S]

Mr. Kahanamoku returns two weeks after spironolactone was added and five days after his sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea, when his potassium was 5.5 mmol/L. He followed the sick-day card: he held empagliflozin, furosemide, spironolactone and sacubitril-valsartan, took half-dose carvedilol for two days and drank oral rehydration solution. The illness settled after three days, and he restarted all his medicines two days ago. His home weight is 93 kg and steady, he has no swelling, orthopnea or lightheadedness, and he walks a mile on the flat without stopping. He is eager to be back in the ocean and asks how to do it safely. [S]

list.item:
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (I50.22). Euvolemic at a dry weight of about 93 kg, NYHA class II, KCCQ-12 66. Potassium 4.8 mmol/L and creatinine 1.20 mg/dL (eGFR 67) two days after restarting, back near baseline, so the sick-day rules worked. Pulse 68 and blood pressure 112/70 allow a beta-blocker increase; one change at a time after the illness. [S]
Raise carvedilol to 12.5 mg twice daily.
Reduce furosemide to 20 mg daily now that he is dry.
Raise sacubitril-valsartan to 49/51 mg twice daily in two weeks by the heart failure nurse, with a metabolic panel one week after that change.
Continue empagliflozin and spironolactone 12.5 mg.

Coronary artery disease (I25.2). LDL 62 mg/dL six weeks after atorvastatin was raised to 80 mg, at goal; ALT 31 U/L. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 80 mg and aspirin 81 mg.

Exercise and the ocean. He will be eligible for cardiac rehabilitation for heart failure in about four weeks, six weeks after his angiography and his last new medicine. [S]
Cardiac rehabilitation, 36 sessions, from late May, with pool swimming once the team agrees.
Until then, walking only; no swimming or surfing yet.
Ocean plan after rehabilitation: calm water inside the reef, with a companion and near a lifeguard; no breath-hold diving; no big surf until cleared; water through the morning; out of the water at once for chest pain, lightheadedness or unusual breathlessness.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure (2022); 2024 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway for Treatment of Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction (2024); 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, heart failure and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Heart failure nurse call in two weeks to raise sacubitril-valsartan, with a metabolic panel one week later. Cardiac rehabilitation from late May. Annual wellness visit in September; heart failure review in about five months with a repeat echocardiogram. Next scheduled visit 1957-09-14: subsequent annual wellness visit. [S]
